pages:
Great. A wonderful morning Atsushi was having.

Atsushi walked around the white building that seemed too bright to be comforting. His bruised body wasn't helping either.

After a painful stomach ache from eating Chazuke last night to having to wake up at 4am to fight along side the very man who wanted to rip off his limbs.

Atsushi went up to the exhausted looking lady at the reception as he struggled to find the right room where that Rashōmon-guy was.

Well, as much as he felt that Akutagawa was a man with a sense of morality as much as that of a generic villain, he couldn't ignore the dread building up in his very stomach at the feeling that something was very wrong.

Or maybe it was the Chazuke dancing in his stomach.

As he stopped infront of the room, he pulled the scarf he had around his neck tighter.

It's colder than it should be today.

Room 4

Atsushi seemed to want to turn back and run away (and maybe get some rest). His body was throbbing with pain, his heart was doing these weird flips that made his decision to visit Akutagawa at the hospital seem stupid.

"Right, it's a hospital.", Atsushi thought to himself. He knew it was a hospital from the very moment he stepped in. But maybe, just maybe the realisation was sinking in now, since the adrenaline from the battle they fought earlier this morning was fading.

He couldn't back off from this now. He had to see how Akutagawa was on the Agency's behalf.

Atsushi looked at the door blankly, then he looked around himself.

"It's....quite empty...today", Atsushi said to himself, nearly scaring a small child next to him as he spoke to no one in particular.

Atsushi took a deep breath before a nurse went into the room quickly after quite literally shoving Atsushi aside. And what Atsushi heard was.... suprising...

If Atsushi's ears hadn't been damaged then he probably heard someone cry.

Atsushi could not believe his ears. Maybe he was infront of the wrong room? He took a look at the clock shortly, briefly noting it was 7:23am before re-checking the room he's supposed to be in.

It is the room he's supposed to see Akutagawa in.

He took a hesitant step before quickly turning the knob and stepping in.

Atsushi's jaw dropped. All the pain from his stomach was gone. But now, his heart was aching, and still doing weird flips.

chapitres.titre: Chapter 2: Tears of Someone You Don't Know
pages:
Atsushi's stomach flipped.

Akutagawa was the one crying.

It shouldn't have been funny, but Atsushi could not help but feel very conscious of his growing urge to laugh.

"NO–Get a hold of yourself, Atsush-", Atsushi thought to himself. He nearly let out a weird suppressed type of sound that would've sounded suspiciously like a laugh.

And would've gotten his limbs ripped right off from Akutagawa's ability if he had heard it.

It's just that Akutagawa's eyes were puffy and red, kind of like a fish's. He had this weird pout that didn't match quite match what Atsushi thought of him.

Atsushi felt the corners of his lips twitch.

Atsushi always felt bad for people, it wasn't anything new.

But this was the first time when it ached so much that his heart started racing, but he also felt like laughing.

Well- he must've looked stupid just standing there because Akutagawa gave him a sharp glare.

It didn't really intimidate Atsushi. Akutagawa looked like a child who cried, and is upset and now is trying to be threatening.

Akutagawa sniffled and wiped the tears away which only made it worse for Atsushi because Akutagawa might've pulled that poker face back on, but his shoulders were trembling uncontrollably.

"Were-tiger."

Atsushi looked at Akutagawa since he knew Akutagawa was far from ever using Atsushi's name. He walked forward and sat down beside the hospital bed. (Not without keeping a slight distance in case he needed to dodge a Rashōmon attack)

Atsushi dumbly stared into Akutagawa's eyes, it was only when Akutagawa's eyes hardened that he remembered to respond.

"What?", Atsushi said. It still felt like a fever dream. The early morning fight, this visit to the hospital, and most importantly Akutagawa's tears.

Akutagawa stared into the distance quietly.

No.

Something was wrong.

A feeling of weird nausea crept up in Atsushi's stomach.

Akutagawa usually retorted the second someone said something.

And it was cold and hazy all over again for Atsushi like it has been earlier this morning.

"I cannot hear you", Akutagawa said as he shifted his gaze from the distance to his hands in his lap.

"What?", Atsushi said. It was hard to process.

Atsushi needed a rewind button to go back and observe everything before this all took place.

Akutagawa did not respond. He didn't hear Atsushi at all.

He sunk back into the bed.

Atsushi stared at the floor, doing everything to avoid Akutagawa's eyes—who was doing the same thing.

Atsushi felt a disgusting feeling of hatred towards his observation skills when he noticed Akutagawa's bandaged ear.

It looked awful.

It looked like the war had been cut off clean and blood had went inside the ear and dried there as far as Atsushi's knowledge could go.

It might've be beyond that. But Atsushi was no longer paying attention, he wanted nothing more than to get up, walk out and wait before coming back in until everything went back to normal.

Atsushi didn't think before he acted, the nausea and possibly the Chazuke dancing in his stomach made his brain foggy; his hand reached out and his fingertip brushed against Akutagawa's under eye and his finger just gently grazed Akutagawa's skin near his cheekbone where the dried tears were.

For someone who looks so pale, and sickly, Akutagawa's skin was surprisingly soft. It felt like Atsushi's finger tips brushed against a flower's petal rather than a human's skin.

Atsushi had expected a slap to his hand, and even an assault from Rashōmon.

But what he didn't expect was to feel warm tears crawling down his fingers and wrist.

It was a blur.

Akutagawa was trembling, warm tears crawled down Atsushi's wrist—he could make out the sound of the sobs. But it was barely there.

Atsushi was lost.

He didn't know the person infront of him.

Atsushi has gotten himself into huge trouble, hadn't he?

The cold room felt so quiet that Atsushi might've assumed that he had also gone deaf if it weren't for the sound of the AC humming softly.

Usually, the sound of AC was comforting to Atsushi. Yet today, it was irksome.

He wanted nothing more than to turn it off.

He was getting irritated and irritated. He wanted to peel the skin off of his hands–

That is until he heard a muffled cough from a few feets behind him that made him snap back and realise that he was still washing his hands.

Scrubbing harshly, no less.

If he didn't stop it, the he might ACTUALLY tear his skin off.

He turned the faucet off and turned to look at Akutagawa who refused to meet Atsushi's eyes.

"So....want an apple?", Atsushi asked as if Akutagawa's dead ears could catch his voice at all.

Akutagawa probably saw Atsushi's lips move and gave the stare of the deepest disgust as if reminding him that he was deaf now.

Atsushi realised it and stood there stiffly.

Yea.

Things were still awkward.

Seeing Akutagawa cry was definitely not on his bingo card.

Atsushi sighed heavily before grabbing an apple from the table nearby.

He fixated his gaze on Akutagawa's eye's—the rims slightly red—before tossing the apple to him and looking away as if disturbed to meet Akutagawa's red rimmed eyes.

Akutagawa did something very strange the moment he brought the apple to his lips.

He smiled slightly.

Just slightly, yet that sent Atsushi's pulse heading to the moon.

Maybe Akutagawa found Atsushi's unease terribly amusing despite his own unease.

And he probably thought Atsushi couldn't see his lips curl up into the slightest, cutest smile behind the apple.

Atsushi was enamored.

Until the night, Atsushi kept secretly wishing to see that smile on Akutagawa's face again.

Atsushi's needn't have stayed this long, yet he found it more comforting to stay in this cold, silent room rather than go back to the agency or his dorm room.

The night finally started consuming any ray of light.

It was quite the star–less sky today....

Atsushi picked up a few snack wrappers from where he and Akutagawa had shared snacks from and sighed before heading out.

Akutagawa probably wished to be alone, poor guy.

It was a bit of greenish–blue in the sky today as Atsushi started to step out...or maybe that was just the affect of having stayed in this room the whole say. So unnatural and unnerving.

Atsushi has barely even took one step towards the door when Akutagawa's voice rang through the entire room.

"....wait,", Akutagawa said.

He struggled to find the rest of his words.

Atsushi didn't want to turn back. He did not wish to stay here for a second more, but how could he not turn around and check what Akutagawa's expression was at the moment when his voice sounded so pleading?

Atsushi knew if he looked back once, he'll not be leaving until the next day. Probably not even that.

Atsushi's legs seemed to be frozen despite him having made up his mind to turn back.

Atsushi sighed and clenched his hands and then dropped them to his sides, completely loose.

He threw the wrappers into the dustbin nearby.

He turned back to see Akutagawa sitting in the shadows of the closed window blinds from where the greenish–blue light, seeping in through the small gaps, reflected onto his eyes.

"Alright, Akutagawa. For just one night."

4:00AM

Atsushi dreamed of nothing as he slept in the wooden chair beside Akutagawa's bed where Akutagawa slept peacefully like a child in his mother's care.

Atsushi's hand, despite feeling the cold skin of Akutagawa's fingers, remained on top of Akutagawa's hand gently.

Barely, messily, but undeniably there.

Atsushi had been getting extremely attached lately.

For the next 2 weeks, he went to work and came back by the evening.

How could he not? Akutagawa actually showed reactions to his words and it was hilarious when he tried to put his walls back up.

And Akutagawa's health was rapidly declining and Atsushi found it hard to not be around Akutagawa that time.

He couldn't leave and not come back.

That had been taking a toll on Atsushi—physically and mentally.

Their interactions were hard to maintain, he had to write everything because Akutagawa couldn't hear.

Sometimes the silence made him nauseous.

Had it not since the very starting?

Atsushi had been neglecting his meals—and it was because of this long stay in this hospital. He felt gravely disturbed by the quiet yet tense atmosphere.

The tense atmosphere made sleep almost impossible. He barely slept a few hours before heading to work.

This had caused him to start taking pills. Anything would go.

Vitamins, numbing pills and all the medication not meant for him.

The warmth from Akutagawa's and his interaction was only limited.

Atsushi wondered if Akutagawa's appetite had also dwindled since being admitted into the hospital.

Atsushi had also had a few interactions with Gin in the past few days because of her visits to her brother Ryunosuke.

The agency members, along with a few Mafia executives, had also noticed Atsushi's constant presence around Akutagawa.

.........

"H-hhuf...."

Tears slipped from his eyes onto his quivering lips.

Atsushi sat in the hospital's restroom's cold and dirty floor with his hands over his head, quivering lips, vision blurred due to the tears and extreme pain in his left fore arm.

This restroom wasn't a functioning one—the right one was next to it.

He felt disgusting. More disgusting than he had ever done in the orphanage.

Blood kept flowing out of the cuts despite it being a few minutes from when they were made.

The small blade rested in Atsushi's numb right palm.

His black gloves were stained with blood and he felt like throwing up out of regret.

Nonetheless, he had to get up and go back to Akutagawa's room.

The rain simply wasn't helping to improve Atsushi's mood.

Atsushi pushed himself off of the wall to get up before realising that the sleeve of his shirt isn't long enough to cover the cuts.

"Shit....", muttered Atsushi. Right now, he felt deep regret and nausea.

And this time, the nausea wasn't because of Chazuke.

Atsushi looked around, his tears had dried but seeing that there's almost no way to hide the cuts, he wanted to cry again.

He needed to cut again and again until it all disappeared.

He needed a way to hide this immediately.

Atsushi found no better way than to keep his arm near his side so the cuts wouldn't be visible.

He was back in the room with Akutagawa and the same warmth but he was caution of his forearm being visible.

Akutagawa kept giving him the worst side eye. He probably had noticed the stiff movements of Atsushi's arm but chose to not comment on it.

How long will Atsushi have to keep this on for?

Akutagawa's coughing attack broke Atsushi out of his thoughts.

"Akuta...gawa...?"

In response Atsushi got an even more severe coughing fit from Akutagawa. Atsushi panicked—he held Akutagawa's face in his hands—his fingers shaking—to try and access the situation.

"W-what.....?"

Atsushi felt blood drip down his arm but it was not the cuts, it was Akutagawa's.

Atsushi panicked as he yelled for help from the nurses.

Akutagawa was bleeding from the mouth, badly at that.

Akutagawa's coughing fit only seemed to get worse as he chocked on the blood that accidentally swept into his throat—he was as startled as Atsushi. Atsushi's forehead was all cold sweat by now.

Atsushi's fingers shook as he gripped Akutagawa's hand tightly and intertwined their fingers together.

The nurse and doctors came rushing to the scene and Atsushi no longer paid any attention to what was happening or the sting in his forearm.

He was numb from the shock. His fingers seemed to drag themselves numbly up against the dried blood on his arm as he traced the cuts there and Akutagawa's blood that he still hadn't the guts to wash off.

His eyes shift up just slightly as he watched his fingers drag lightly across the cuts on his arm. He didn't feel any sadness like he usually did. He felt nauseous and frustrated.

He realised that he was sitting on the cold floor outside the room where Akutagawa was being treated—the 18 old boy was curled up like an upset child with his legs close to his chest and his arms around his legs—only when Gin stood beside him, she was also drenched in cold sweat.

Looks like she had ran all the way here for her brother.

That thought really just made Atsushi more numb.

"Must be nice to have someone who really cares about you like that", he thought as he mindlessly gazed at Gin who stood nervously beside Atsushi while fidgeting with her shirt.

"Do I care about Akutagawa?"

Atsushi had been asking himself that question ever since the first night he decided to stay with Akutagawa.

But he knew Akutagawa probably didn't feel the same about him.

The next fews days were a blur.

Atsushi didn't know what he was doing, but neither did he want to.

Akutagawa was in an extremely fragile state and kept under the influence a lot of medicines with no visitors allowed due to his state.

Atsushi felt as if worms were crawling in his chest. He could no longer sleep, eat or even move anymore.

He felt grateful that he has this excuse to finally go back to his dorm room.

But the dorm room didn't feel his. He took a step inside and saw Kyouka at the dining table eating tofu. She opened her mouth as if to say something but Atsushi merely opened the huge cupboard and crawled into the lower part.

Beads of sweat began forming or his forehead. He was being childish. He did want to talk to people but he simply didn't know how to use his mouth.

He felt uncomfortable in his own body, nothing felt right. The appreciation he got after accomplishing his missions no longer brought joy to him but only worsened his misery.

Soon he buried his face in his knees and felt tears spill down his face for no reason. He tensed up because he sobbed because he knew Kyouka could hear him.

Kyouka didn't dare confront Atsushi about it the next day but simply told him that Akutagawa was allowed to have visitors again.

That was supposed to bring Atsushi joy?

Atsushi heard that and stared at Kyouka for long before smiling softly. He felt as if the hair on his neck were sticking to his skin purposefully to make him uncomfortable.

He wanted to tear his skin off, he wanted to cry and throw a tantrum and tell people how he couldn't handle something he didn't even recognise.

Pressure? Irritability? Frustration? Grief? Pain?

He didn't even know. He didn't even feel valid enough to feel this way.

After all, it was not him in the hospital.

Regardless of how he felt he still went to the hospital. He stood out of that exact door he knew Akutagawa was in, but the door no longer felt familiar.

It felt as if Atsushi knew this place from a dream.

His sweaty hand pressed against the door's knob before he twisted it and stepped inside.

Akutagawa looked weaker than ever, but he was smiling. The same smile Atsushi had wished to see for a while did not seem to do anything.

Atsushi's eyes immediately shifted to Akutagawa's ears. Atsushi could feel himself tensing up with a feeling of nausea. Then, as his sweaty hand pressed against his thigh he looked at Akutagawa and spoke abruptly.

"Ryunosuke, I love you."

chapitres.titre: Chapter 7: Regret and His Way To Put An End To It
pages:
Atsushi could no longer stand the way Akutagawa looked at him as if wanting to remind him that he couldn't hear.

Atsushi's eyes darted from tile to tile as he stared down at the floor trying to push back the tears that formed.

Atsushi's clothes clung to his body uneasily which made him want to tear his skin off. It was as if everything in his body was hurting just to make him uncomfortable.

Atsushi turned back to leave despite the pit of his stomach wanting to collapse and his guts wanting to spill open through his stomach.

"Atsushi"

Akutagawa let out a pathetic squeak as his voice quivered and tears slid down his cheeks as he tried to push Atsushi's name out of his mouth without feeling a bitter taste after it.

Atsushi turned around—his movements were no longer quick or panicked. They were sluggish and lazy.

The black of Atsushi's pupils swallowed his purple and yellow iris as he looked up to see Akutagawa in such a state.

It made Atsushi beyond nauseous.

"W-would you....stop?...trying to leave?.."

Akutagawa forced out as he looked Atsushi with something Atsushi couldn't identify.

Akutagawa tried to recollect himself and fix this pathetic state of his but to no avail the tears kept falling.

Atsushi's hands hung limply by his side—no longer were they pressed up against his thigh.

Atsushi rushed over to Akutagawa and his hands immediately cupped Akutagawa's cheeks as his bottom lip started to quiver and his eyes started watering.

For some reason, Akutagawa felt his tears stop and dry on his cheek. Atsushi's tears simply discouraged Akutagawa's tears to continue slide down his face.

Atsushi desperately cradled Akutagawa's face in his hands.

"Your...words that I never heard—were they important?"

Atsushi felt his gut sink somewhere to the wrong position.

"I could never bring myself to say them to you—or write them to you"

Akutagawa stared up Atsushi.

This time, he didn't question Atsushi speaking instead of explaining things by writting them down.

As if sensing Atsushi's upcoming movement, he reached for Atsushi's hand but Atsushi had already pulled away.

The bright yellow in his eyes felt dull and the purple seemed to be almost black.

Before Akutagawa could even let the words out, Atsushi ran out of the room faster than he had ever did in his life.

He wished he wouldn't have done.

He wished he could undo this.

This would only end up as his biggest and last regret.

Atsushi stood before Akutagawa's limp body on the hospital bed. His pale face was whiter than ever and the barely remaining fat on his skin was even more prominent under that hospital gown.

Atsushi shifted the bouquet of white lilies in his hand before he walked over to a nurse in the room.

Atsushi has a soft look on his face that surprised the nurse who had been gathering Akutagawa's belongings such as his jabot.

"Do you require something, sir?"

Atsushi had been the sole person allowed in here besides the Port Mafia members at the moment. Akutagawa was once again abandoned by all except Gin who could not bring herself to enter the room where Akutagawa's soul-less body lay and had requested to see him only once before his burial.

Even Atsushi had abandoned Akutagawa at that moment.

That was the guilt he'd always carry.

"I need some time alone here...just a few minutes...it will take no longer than 5"

Atsushi said as he tilted his head to the side, smiling softly.

The nurse was quite startled by his request because she thought he'd ask for something like his belongings—not a moment to be alone with a lifeless body in a cold hospital room.

The nurse couldn't bring herself to speak as she took in Atsushi's bitter smile and soft eyes. She swiftly nodded and left the room.

Atsushi felt worse now that he was alone in this cold that he had probably also left Akutagawa in.

He walked over and placed the bouquet beside Akutagawa's head on the bed.

He took a full minute staring at Akutagawa as if memorizing his features for the next birth.

He felt light. Unbearably light as if something was about to finally bring him peace.

He walked over to the window and opened it. A gush of silent gentle breeze flew in ruffling his bangs and hair strands just slightly almost with a refreshing sensation on his face.

He looked over his shoulder at Akutagawa's body just one last time before he lifted himself up and his fingers automatically grasped the window frame as he looked down to the busy roads of Yokohama.

Had he ever noticed just how high up this floor was before?

It had been raining heavily before, and light rain that was nearing it's end, fell down like transparent arrows from the cupid in the sky.

The sun had risen. It was odd.

It was so bright yet so unnervingly and warmly shadowy that Atsushi almost couldn't explain what the water exactly was.

It was a depressing shade of bright blue in the sky. Clouds floated above aimlessly, changing with the movement.

Atsushi felt his lips tug upwards into the softest smile at the same time as his eyelids dropped gently as his fingers slipped themselves free from the window frame and his feet finally losing the feeling of solid wood below.

He felt the soft warmth of the sun above and the coolness of the gentle breeze before he finally let his eyes close and let all his memories go with him.

His love would always remain in his memories if not his words.
